story.iWant: create and configure multiple bots within my organization
story.soThat: I can separate knowledge bases by department or use case

task.title: Create POST /api/v1/bots endpoint
task.details: Accept name (required), description (optional), confidence_threshold (default 80). Validate name length, uniqueness within tenant, threshold range 0-100. Return bot object with id, name, description, confidence_threshold, status, created_at. Enforce tenant isolation (RLS) and authenticated user. Audit log bot creation.

task.title: Create bots table migration
task.details: Schema: id (UUID PK), tenant_id (UUID FK indexed), name (VARCHAR 2-50 NOT NULL), description (VARCHAR max 500), confidence_threshold (INT 0-100 default 80), status (ENUM: Empty/Processing/Ready, default Empty), created_at (TIMESTAMP), updated_at (TIMESTAMP), created_by (UUID FK). Constraints: unique(tenant_id, name), RLS policy, indexes on tenant_id and (tenant_id, created_at).

task.title: Create GET/PATCH bot endpoints
task.details: GET /api/v1/bots/{bot_id} returns complete bot object with RLS enforcement. PATCH /api/v1/bots/{bot_id} accepts name/description/confidence_threshold with validation and audit logging. GET /api/v1/bots (list) with query params: limit (default 20), offset, sort_by (name/created_at), search (name). Return paginated list with total_count and enforce RLS.

task.title: Implement bot limit enforcement
task.details: Add subscription_tier column to tenants table (free/pro/enterprise, default free). Define limits: free=5, pro=25, enterprise=unlimited. In POST /bots, check current bot count vs limit before creation. Return 402 Limit Exceeded with error message if at limit.

task.title: Create Bot List page component
task.details: Path: apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/bots/page.tsx. Include BotListHeader (title, "Create Bot" button, search), BotCard (name, description, doc count, threshold, actions), BotGrid (paginated). Features: fetch via GET /api/v1/bots?limit=20&offset=0, real-time debounced search (300ms), pagination, sorting (name/created date), responsive mobile layout. Handle loading/error states with skeletons and error banner.

task.title: Create CreateBotModal component
task.details: Path: apps/web/src/components/CreateBotModal.tsx. Fields: Name input (required 2-50 chars), Description textarea (optional max 500 with char counter), Confidence threshold slider (0-100%). Real-time validation with live uniqueness check (debounced API call). Submit disabled until valid. Show loading during submission and inline error display. On success close modal, add to list, show toast. On error show inline messages.

task.title: Create BotSettingsModal component
task.details: Path: apps/web/src/components/BotSettingsModal.tsx. Load bot details on mount via GET /api/v1/bots/{bot_id}. Display all fields with editable name/description/threshold and read-only id/created_at. Field validation same as create. Save triggers PATCH with optimistic updates. Show loading indicator. Handle server errors inline. Copy bot ID to clipboard feature.

task.title: Create custom React hooks for bots
task.details: Create useBotsQuery() for list fetching, useBotQuery(botId) for single bot details, useCreateBot() mutation for POST, useUpdateBot(botId) for PATCH, useDeleteBot(botId) for DELETE (future). Implement optimistic updates. Handle loading/error/success states. Manage pagination state. Use TanStack Query (React Query) or SWR. Paths: apps/web/src/hooks/useBotsQuery.ts, useCreateBot.ts, useUpdateBot.ts.

task.title: Create bot API client functions
task.details: Path: apps/web/src/lib/api/bots.ts. Functions: createBot(name, description, threshold), listBots(limit, offset, search, sort), getBotDetails(botId), updateBot(botId, updates), deleteBot(botId). Include proper error handling and type safety.

task.title: Define TypeScript bot types
task.details: Path: apps/web/src/types/bot.ts. Types: Bot (id, name, description, confidence_threshold, status, created_at, updated_at, doc_count), CreateBotInput, UpdateBotInput, PaginatedBotsResponse.

task.title: Write pytest tests for bot endpoints
task.details: Path: apps/api/tests/test_bots.py. Test POST /bots: valid input, invalid name (length), duplicate name, unauthenticated, at limit, RLS isolation. Test GET /bots: list all bots, pagination, search filter, RLS isolation. Test GET /bots/{id}: correct bot details, RLS forbidden. Test PATCH /bots/{id}: name/description/threshold updates with validation, RLS enforcement.

task.title: Write Vitest/RTL tests for bot components
task.details: Path: apps/web/__tests__/BotListPage.test.tsx and component tests. Test BotListPage: render with list, mock API calls, search filtering, pagination, modal open. Test CreateBotModal: form rendering, name validation, uniqueness check, threshold slider, submit disabled until valid, success/error handling. Test BotSettingsModal: load details, edit fields, submit, toast, error handling, copy to clipboard.

task.title: Write Playwright E2E integration test
task.details: User logs in → navigates to Bots page → clicks "Create Bot" → fills form (name="HR Bot", description, threshold=75) → submits → bot appears in list → clicks bot to open settings → updates name to "HR Bot v2" → saves → name updates in list → test free tier limit (create 5 bots, 6th fails with 402).

task.title: Update README and API docs
task.details: Update README.md with bot management feature overview. Document API endpoints: POST/GET/PATCH /bots with request/response examples. Add database schema diagram for bots table. Include frontend architecture notes: component hierarchy and state flow. Add curl/code snippets for API examples.

acceptanceCriteria.criteria: User can navigate to Bots page from dashboard
User can click "Create Bot" button
Create Bot form displays with fields: Name (required, 2-50 chars, unique per org), Description (optional, max 500 chars), Confidence threshold slider (0-100%, default 80%)
Form validates in real-time: Name min 2 / max 50 chars, Unique constraint checked live, Description max 500 chars, Confidence threshold numeric 0-100
When submitting valid form: New bot record created with status "Empty", Bot assigned to current tenant, User redirected to bot's Knowledge Base page, Bot appears in list
Success toast: "Bot created: [Bot Name]"
User sees empty state: "No documents uploaded. Upload your first document to get started."
User can view all bots they own in their organization
Bot list displays: Bot name (clickable), Description preview (truncated), Document count, Last updated date, Confidence threshold value, Actions button (Settings, Duplicate, Delete)
Bot list supports pagination (20 per page)
Bots sortable by: name, created date, last updated
User can search bots by name (case-insensitive)
User can click "Settings" on any bot
Settings modal displays: Name (editable), Description (editable, max 500 chars), Confidence threshold (slider 0-100%), Bot ID (read-only, copyable), Created date (read-only)
User can edit name and description
Name must remain unique within organization (live validation)
User can adjust confidence threshold
Changes saved immediately on field blur or button click
User sees success toast: "Settings updated"
Validation errors display inline
Organization's bot limit enforced per subscription tier
When user hits bot limit, "Create Bot" button disabled with tooltip: "You've reached your bot limit. Upgrade to create more."
Free tier: 5 bots max, Pro tier: 25 bots max, Enterprise: unlimited
If bot name not unique: "Bot name already exists in your organization"
If invalid input: specific field validation message
If submission fails: "Failed to create bot. Please try again."
If reached bot limit: "You've reached your bot limit. Upgrade to create more."

artifact.title: Technical Specification
artifact.snippet: RLS (Row Level Security): All tables must have tenant_id. Session: Inject tenant_id into PostgreSQL session on every request. Vector Store: Use pgvector for embeddings with IVFFlat index for performance.

artifact.title: Technical Specification
artifact.snippet: Frontend: Next.js 14 (App Router), TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui. Backend: FastAPI (Python 3.11+), Pydantic, SQLAlchemy (Async). Database: PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector. Auth: NextAuth.js (Frontend) + JWT Validation (Backend).

artifact.title: Architecture Document
artifact.snippet: Mandate: Row-Level Security (RLS) in PostgreSQL + tenant_id context propagation in APIs. Use PostgreSQL + pgvector for MVP and early scale with careful partitioning and tuning.

artifact.title: Epic Breakdown
artifact.snippet: Epic 2 covers Bot & Knowledge Management FR7-FR19. Story 2.1 enables users to create and configure multiple bots for knowledge base separation by department or use case. Includes bot creation, list display, settings, subscription tier limits.

artifact.title: Product Requirements Document
artifact.snippet: FR7: Users can create multiple bots within their organization. FR8: Users can configure bot settings: name, description, confidence threshold. FR9: Users can set the auto-respond confidence threshold. FR12: Bots are isolated - documents and queries scoped to assigned bot.

constraint.title: RLS Enforcement
constraint.details: All bot queries must include tenant_id filters via PostgreSQL RLS policies. Pattern: tenant_id = current_setting('app.current_tenant_id')::uuid. Enforce at database layer, not application layer.

constraint.title: JWT Authentication
constraint.details: All bot endpoints require valid JWT token in Authorization header. Token must be validated via existing AuthService from apps/api/app/core/security.py. Tenant ID extracted from JWT payload and set in session for RLS.

constraint.title: Subscription Tier Limits
constraint.details: Bot creation must enforce subscription tier limits before database insert. Free tier: 5 bots max. Pro: 25. Enterprise: unlimited. Check at API layer and return 402 Limit Exceeded if limit reached.

constraint.title: Name Uniqueness per Tenant
constraint.details: Bot names must be unique within a tenant (not globally). Database unique constraint: (tenant_id, name). Live validation on frontend via debounced API call to check availability before submit.

constraint.title: Status Immutability at Creation
constraint.details: Bot status defaults to "Empty" on creation and is read-only for this story. Future stories will transition status to "Processing" (during document ingestion) and "Ready" (after embeddings complete).

constraint.title: Pagination Defaults
constraint.details: Bot list endpoint default limit: 20 per page. Offset-based pagination (not cursor-based). Support client-side search/sort via query parameters for now; database-side implementation acceptable if performance requires it.

constraint.title: Error Response Format
constraint.details: All error responses must follow consistent Pydantic error schema. 400 for validation errors, 401 for auth, 402 for limit exceeded, 409 for conflict (duplicate name), 403 for RLS forbidden.

constraint.title: Optimistic Updates
constraint.details: Frontend state updates should assume success before server response to minimize perceived latency. Revert on error and display error toast. Apply to bot creation and settings updates.

standards.paragraph: Backend tests use pytest with FastAPI TestClient for endpoint testing. Follow existing auth test patterns in Story 1-4: mock JWT tokens with tenant_id in payload, use fixtures for authenticated clients. All database tests must verify RLS enforcement by confirming queries return only current-tenant data and forbidden access for other tenants. Frontend tests use Vitest + React Testing Library with mocked API calls via MSW (Mock Service Worker) or simple fetch mocks. E2E tests use Playwright with user-level flows: login, navigate, interact with forms, verify DOM updates. All tests must be isolated and non-flaky (deterministic, no external service dependencies).

idea.description: Test POST /bots: verify new bot created with status "Empty", assigned to tenant, and returned in response with correct fields (id, name, description, confidence_threshold, created_at).

Test real-time form validation: type invalid name lengths (1 char, 51 chars), verify error message updates immediately without form submission. Test threshold slider out of range (negative, >100), verify error.
Test name uniqueness: create bot "HR Bot", attempt to create second bot with same name, verify 409 Conflict response with message "Bot name already exists in your organization".

Test free tier bot limit: create 5 bots successfully, attempt 6th bot, verify 402 Limit Exceeded response. Verify "Create Bot" button disabled and tooltip shows "You've reached your bot limit. Upgrade to create more."
Test RLS isolation: create bots in tenant A, verify user from tenant B cannot see them via GET /bots or direct GET /bots/{id}. Verify 403 Forbidden on cross-tenant access.
Test pagination: GET /bots?limit=20&offset=0 returns first 20 bots and total_count. Verify offset=20 returns next page. Verify limit parameter respected.
Test search filter: create bots "HR Bot", "IT Bot", "Sales Bot". Search "HR" returns only "HR Bot". Search is case-insensitive ("hr" matches "HR Bot").

Test BotSettingsModal: update bot name to "Updated Name", verify changes reflected in modal and list immediately (optimistic). Verify success toast "Settings updated" appears. Test name uniqueness validation live in settings form.
Test "Create Bot" button opens modal with empty form. Test modal opens from dashboard button and from bot list actions menu. Verify modal is reusable.
Test empty state: newly created bot shows empty state message "No documents uploaded. Upload your first document to get started." on Knowledge Base page.
Test sort options: fetch bots, apply sort_by=name, verify list sorted alphabetically. Apply sort_by=created_at, verify newest/oldest order (specify ascending/descending if in spec).
